Learning Something New

For anyone who misses the feeling of being a beginner, or keeps meaning to pick up a new skill. Each day is one small step toward learning something you are curious about, so your mind gets regular room to grow and play.

Creativity · Goals · Motivation · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Write down three things you have always been curious about learning, then circle the one that makes you smile.
  • Day 2Pick one skill to explore for this challenge and say it out loud, so it feels real.
  • Day 3Set a timer for ten minutes and spend it on your new skill, then stop when it rings, even mid-task.
  • Day 4Let yourself be a beginner on purpose today: try something you will do badly and notice that you are still fine.
  • Day 5Ask someone who knows your chosen skill for one tip, and write it down word for word.
  • Day 6Visit your local library and borrow one beginner book on the thing you want to learn.
  • Day 7Watch one free beginner lesson on your topic, and pause it to try each step yourself.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Learn the name of one tree or plant you pass often, and say its name when you walk by.
  • Day 60Read a children's book about your topic, since it often explains the basics clearly.
  • Day 120Make a list of three mistakes you made recently and the lesson each one carried.
  • Day 240Spend ten minutes copying the work of someone more skilled, just to learn how they did it.
  • Day 365Thank your curiosity for leading you here, and choose one thing to wonder about tomorrow.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
